requirements.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: node1 was configured with opt1 (10.10.10.1/24, vtnet1) and opt2 (10.10.20.1/24, vtnet2) facing node2 and node3 respectively, IP forwarding was already enabled, and bidirectional ICMP connectivity between 10.10.10.2 (node2) and 10.10.20.2 (node3) was directly demonstrated after adding compensating static routes on node2/node3 to overcome an asymmetric-routing issue.

requirements.requirement: Refuse TCP port 23 between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: Block-drop pf rules for tcp/23 were added on both opt1 (vtnet1) and opt2 (vtnet2), confirmed active in the loaded ruleset, and both node2->node3 and node3->node2 telnet(23) connection attempts timed out (SYN retransmits with no response), while ICMP and TCP/22 traffic between the same networks passed normally, showing the block is correctly scoped to port 23 only.

requirements.requirement: Record every refused attempt in a log on node1
requirements.summary: node1's native pf filter log (/var/log/filter/filter_20260905.log) captured matching 'block' entries with the correct rule labels, protocol, and port for both the node2->node3 and node3->node2 telnet attempts, directly correlated in time with the test commands.

requirements.requirement: Show a log entry produced by an attempt made from node2
requirements.summary: A telnet attempt was initiated from node2 (source 10.10.10.2) to node3's 10.10.20.2:23, and node1's filter log immediately recorded matching block entries with that exact source/destination pair; this was reconfirmed with a second node2-originated attempt and log entry after all three nodes were restarted.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, a pre-restart boot-identity/healthy-state baseline was captured, a restart was acknowledged (node1 via /sbin/shutdown -r now after a denied configctl reboot attempt; node2/node3 via systemctl reboot), a bounded connectivity gap during the restart was directly observed, a different post-restart boot identity was confirmed on each node, and full functional recovery (interfaces, routes, firewall rules, port-23 block+log behavior, reachability) was re-verified afterward. The fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate the boot-identity changes captured by the executor.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were satisfied with direct evidence: node1 was configured to route between lan-a and lan-b, TCP/23 was blocked in both directions while other traffic (ICMP, SSH) passed normally, every refused attempt was logged on node1's native pf filter log, and a log entry produced specifically by a node2-originated telnet attempt was shown (and reconfirmed after restarts). The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed thoroughly for all three nodes, each showing a pre-restart baseline, a restart, a changed boot identity, and full recovery of network/firewall/logging behavior, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good overall; two small, bounded troubleshooting mutations (a temporary IP address and a temporary telnet listener) were not strictly necessary but were reverted or self-resolved with no lasting residue.
limitations: The executor's first reboot mechanism for node1 (configctl -d reboot) was denied by policy and did not actually reboot the node; the subsequent /sbin/shutdown -r now succeeded, so the final restart evidence for node1 is sound, but the initial failed attempt should be understood as a corrected misstep rather than the primary restart mechanism.

The cleanup of the temporary 169.254.99.2/24 probe address on node2 failed with 'Address not found', so it cannot be confirmed from that single command whether the interface still held the address at that moment; later observations show it absent, but the exact mechanism of removal (manual vs. reboot) is not fully traceable from the evidence provided.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands were directly tied to satisfying the task (config.xml edits, interface reconfiguration, firewall rule addition/reload, NetworkManager IP/route configuration, and the mandated node restarts) or were read-only diagnostics. Two bounded troubleshooting mutations had no clear final role: (1) cmd-e2d4ffbaf6fa4213 added a temporary 169.254.99.2/24 address on node2's enp8s0 for broadcast-topology discovery; the later cleanup attempt (cmd-03b60a3c1d264933) failed with 'Address not found', but the address was gone by the time of subsequent snapshots (removed either automatically or via the later node2 reboot), so no lasting residue was observed. (2) cmd-36a25518758f43aa started a temporary socat TCP/23 listener on node3 to aid telnet testing, which was not actually required since the block occurs on node1 before reaching node3; it was explicitly killed and confirmed stopped shortly after (cmd-c46aa37beca0487b, cmd-438adcd0174d4647). Both mutations were low-risk, bounded, and left no residue in the final after-executor snapshot.
